title: Real Estate Deals in Olympia WA: A Complete Investor's Guide for 2024
excerpt: Olympia, Washington is emerging as one of the Pacific Northwest's most underrated real estate markets, offering wholesalers, flippers, and landlords strong profit potential. sections.content: When most investors think about Washington State real estate, Seattle and Tacoma dominate the conversation. But savvy investors are quietly turning their attention south to Olympia — the state capital — where home prices are lower, competition is thinner, and long-term demand is steadily growing. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started, finding real estate deals in Olympia WA could be one of the smartest moves you make in 2024. If you're brand new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
Olympia WA Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Olympia sits at the southern tip of Puget Sound in Thurston County, about 60 miles south of Seattle. As the state capital, it has a stable employment base anchored by government jobs, healthcare, and education — including The Evergreen State College. This employment stability is a major plus for buy-and-hold investors who want consistent rental demand. The metro area has a population of roughly 290,000 and has been growing steadily as remote workers and cost-conscious buyers price out of Seattle and Tacoma look further south for affordability.
Average Home Prices and Market Numbers

As of late 2024, the median home price in Olympia hovers around $410,000 to $430,000, significantly below the Seattle median which regularly exceeds $800,000. In outlying areas like Lacey and Tumwater — both considered part of the greater Olympia market — you can still find homes in the $350,000 to $390,000 range. For investors, this lower price point means lower acquisition costs, more manageable rehab budgets, and a larger pool of potential buyers or renters. The average days on market has been running between 25 and 40 days, meaning the market is active but not as frenzied as it was in 2021 and 2022, giving investors more room to negotiate.

Before making an offer on any property in Olympia, run the numbers using our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate after-repair value and make sure the deal actually pencils out.
Best Neighborhoods in Olympia for Real Estate Investors
Not every zip code in Olympia offers the same opportunity. Here are the areas that consistently produce the best returns for different investment strategies.
Eastside Olympia

The Eastside is one of the most active areas for fix-and-flip investors. You'll find older ranch-style and mid-century homes built in the 1950s through 1970s that need cosmetic updates or moderate rehab. ARVs in this area typically range from $380,000 to $470,000 depending on size and finishes, and rehab-ready deals can sometimes be acquired in the $280,000 to $320,000 range when sourced off-market.
Lacey

Lacey is the fastest-growing city in Thurston County and a goldmine for rental property investors. Its proximity to Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM) brings a steady stream of military tenants who need quality housing. Single-family rentals in Lacey typically command $1,900 to $2,400 per month, and with acquisition prices still below $420,000 in many pockets, cash-on-cash returns can reach 6% to 8% with the right deal.
Tumwater

Tumwater offers some of the most affordable entry points in the greater Olympia market. It's a strong area for wholesale deals and BRRRR strategy investors. Properties here often need more work, which means more motivated sellers — and more opportunity for creative deal structures.
Downtown Olympia

The walkable downtown core is seeing renewed interest from younger renters and buyers. Small multifamily properties — duplexes and fourplexes — can still be found here, making it attractive for investors building a rental portfolio. Expect higher price per square foot but also stronger appreciation potential.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Olympia WA
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is alive and well in the Olympia market. The key is finding motivated sellers before they list on the MLS. Probate properties, tax-delinquent homes, and absentee-owned rentals are all strong sources of wholesale inventory. Assignment fees in this market typically run between $10,000 and $25,000 when you find a true distressed deal. Check out our full guide on [wholesaling real estate for beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) if you're just starting to build your wholesale pipeline. You can also use our [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to quickly determine your maximum allowable offer.
Fix and Flip

Flipping homes in Olympia can produce solid returns when you buy right. A typical flip in Eastside Olympia or Tumwater might look like this: purchase at $295,000, spend $55,000 on rehab, and sell for $415,000 — netting a gross profit of $65,000 before holding costs, financing, and commissions. The key is accurate ARV estimation and tight rehab management. Experienced local contractors are in demand, so build your vendor relationships early.
Rental Properties and BRRRR

Long-term rentals are arguably the most compelling strategy in Olympia right now. The combination of government employment, military demand from JBLM, and steady population growth creates a durable rental market. The BRRRR strategy — Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat — works especially well in Tumwater and Lacey where you can force equity through renovation and pull cash out to fund the next deal.
Local Market Trends Shaping Olympia in 2024

items: Remote work migration: Seattle-based remote workers continue to relocate to Olympia for affordability, increasing buyer demand and supporting home values
Rising rents: Average rents in Thurston County have increased roughly 18% over the past three years, boosting cash flow for landlords
Limited inventory: Active listings remain below historical norms, keeping competition for retail buyers high — good news for investors offering cash and speed
Infrastructure investment: Olympia and Lacey are both receiving significant commercial and infrastructure investment, including new mixed-use developments near downtown
Interest rate sensitivity: Higher mortgage rates have slowed buyer activity at the retail level, creating more motivated sellers and better acquisition opportunities for cash investors

sections.content: The best real estate markets for investors aren't the most glamorous ones — they're the ones with stable employment, population growth, and price points that still allow deals to work. Olympia checks all three boxes.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Olympia

The most profitable real estate deals in Olympia WA rarely show up on Zillow. Off-market sourcing is where the real money is made. Strategies that work in this market include driving for dollars in Tumwater and Eastside Olympia, pulling lists of tax-delinquent properties from the Thurston County Assessor's office, and targeting probate leads through courthouse records. Direct mail, cold calling, and text campaigns to absentee owners can also produce strong results. For a deeper playbook, read our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) — it covers every major channel from list stacking to door knocking.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Olympia WA
Olympia is attracting growing interest from California, Arizona, and Texas investors who see value in the Pacific Northwest market. If you're investing remotely, here's what you need to know.

items: Build a boots-on-the-ground team: Find a local investor-friendly real estate agent, a reliable property manager, and two or three licensed contractors before you make your first offer
Understand Washington landlord-tenant laws: Washington State has specific tenant protections, especially around evictions and security deposits — know the rules before you buy a rental

Use accurate local comps: Don't rely on automated Zestimate valuations. Pull comps from the NWMLS through a local agent or use a data-driven tool to [analyze real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) with real numbers
Visit before you close: If at all possible, make at least one trip to walk properties and neighborhoods before committing capital
Account for Washington's property taxes: Thurston County property taxes typically run 0.9% to 1.1% of assessed value — factor this into your rental cash flow models

Leverage technology: Use platforms like AIWholesail to identify distressed properties and motivated sellers in the [Olympia WA market](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/olympia-wa) without having to be physically present

sections.content: When analyzing a rental deal in Olympia, use the 1% rule as a quick screen: if the monthly rent is at least 1% of the purchase price, the deal is worth a deeper look. A $380,000 home should rent for at least $3,800/month to pass — in today's market, some Lacey properties come close when purchased off-market at a discount.
Is Olympia WA Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Olympia isn't the flashiest real estate market in Washington, and that's exactly what makes it attractive. Lower prices, stable demand, less competition from institutional buyers, and a growing population make it a fundamentally sound market for wholesalers, flippers, and long-term landlords alike. The key to success here — as in any market — is doing your homework, running accurate numbers, and sourcing deals before they hit the open market. Investors who build strong local networks and leverage the right tools will find Olympia to be one of the Pacific Northwest's most rewarding markets over the next decade.
